title: Harm from what was kept close
literal_meaning: The knife tucked at the waist cuts the throat.
explanation: Something or someone trusted and kept close becomes the source of harm. The dictionary puts the saying beside its figurative sense of cheating.
meaning_odia: ଯାହାକୁ ନିଜର ବୋଲି ଭରସା କରି ପାଖରେ ରଖିଥାଉ, ସେହିଠାରୁ କ୍ଷତି ହେବା। ଏଠାରେ ଛୁରିର ଚିତ୍ରଟି ବିଶ୍ୱାସଭଙ୍ଗକୁ ବୁଝାଏ।
usage_example: A trusted business partner secretly diverts the shop’s receipts. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: Violent imagery describes betrayal; it is not an instruction to harm anyone. The source does not establish a particular origin story.
